args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west and failing health checks, with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 records the failure, the rollback and the recovered health status. It also notes that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
